title: Luis López Méndez (London) to Simón Bolívar, 29 Jan 1819: 15 cipher words read from context by a partial table, read in part

steps.what: Images of ff. 227r-228r fetched from the DataViva public API at 1684 x 1999 px, one request at a time.
All cipher words transcribed from the images: 15 words, 70 signs, 42 with a digit.

Table built from the clear context and the vetting's first reading: 20 symbols cover 69 signs, 0 conflicts in both directions. The table comes from the assumed plaintext, so this tests consistency only. 'cinco meses' corrected to 'cinco veces'.

Second reader, blind, on 3x crops: all 70 letters agree; about 3 of 70 symbols (4%) undecided, all digits. Own script: 0 conflicts. Its shuffle test: 76 of 20,000 without conflict. One search found no source for the jailings. It found the status word and the key claim overstated and 'Maracaibo' a proposal.

Must-fix pass on the images at 4-7x: first m on f. 228r is m1; the 3 on the first i of i3 l e4 l is clear; the last t of t1 l e4 t has an extra stroke, left open. Line numbers recounted: l. 17-18, 23 and 27 on f. 227v.

Plain words swapped among cipher words of equal length, 14 words, 20,000 trials: 62 without conflict, all 62 the true assignment. A mild test. The earlier 'held-out' test is withdrawn: its two words use only symbols already seen.
Within each base letter the plain values rise with the digit (e: b f l r t v y). Not assumed in building the table; supports e6 = v. Not checked by the second reader.
14 of 15 words read as sense, in sentences with the clear text. 'Maracaibo' kept as a guess: its fourth sign is written t, while a = l in all eleven other places.

One web search in Spanish found no edition or decipherment; one search found no source for an imprisonment of López Méndez in London in 1818-19. The rift with MacGregor over recruiting was found. Not reached: Bákula 1949, Archivo del Libertador, Mondolfi.

Integration review of 24 Nov 2026 (AI agent, for the maintainers): escalation checked before the write-up. Siblings: the DataViva sweep had searched López Méndez with cifr/clave/secreta and found no other letter in this table; no clear copy or decipherment in the unit; no known key fits; O'Leary and GL.htm already grepped. Every open piece has an outside blocker (too-short or no-key-material). Read share by cipher words 14 of 15 (0.933); class kept 'read in part' because the words rest on a table built from context, so the short-text floor was not applied.

validation.notes: The 20-symbol table was built from the assumed plaintext of the same 15 words; no held-out text in this table exists, so no statistical validation is possible (shuffle control 62 of 20,000, all the true assignment)

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Nearest category only: a partial table guided by the clear text around the cipher words, fitting the 14 words read, and 69 of the 70 signs, without conflict. It is not a recovered key.
outcome.fraction_read_source: transcription.txt and decryption.txt: 69 of 70 signs have a value; 61 of 70 signs are in the 14 words that read as sense. By words 14 of 15 (read_share 0.933).

texts.label: The 15 cipher words, ff. 227v-228r
texts.summary: Pressing Bolívar for funds, López Méndez says in cipher that he has been jailed five times and released on bail; no other source for this was found. Mac Gregor, he says, has done untold harm to the cause; he joined an expedition of his, for [?Maracaibo], and left it. Mac Gregor is now trying to go to Santafé.
texts.note: Only the bold words are cipher; the clear text is there to give sentences. Editorial repairs are marked {E1}-{E4} in reading.md.

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: Read as sentences 3 Nov 2026. I applied key.tsv to every sign and got the decryption as given: 'he estado preso cinco veces y he salido con fianza', 'mac gregor', 'para mar[?] caibo' and 'santa fe'. Set into the clear text around them, these make sound Spanish sentences, and the English follows them closely. There is one hole. In 'Maracaibo' the fourth sign is t? and not l, the sign used for a everywhere else, so that place name is a context guess and the reading flags it as one. Two weaker points: the 20-symbol table was built from the assumed plaintext and has not been checked against any other letter from López Méndez, though repeat patterns such as Gregor, cinco and veces support it. Also, the clear-text word is 'podria' in reading.md but 'podrá' in the transcription comments, which does not affect the cipher words.

outcome.notes: Corrects the catalogue's vetting reading 'cinco meses': the third and fifth signs are m1 and t3, two symbols, so 'meses' does not fit. The jailings rest on the cipher alone. Prior art is open, so first_break is not set.

prior.where: The catalogue's vetting of 28 Oct 2026 (research/latam_vetting/1523_sample.txt) gave a first context reading, with 'cinco meses'. Otherwise none found: not on DECODE or cryptiana, no hit in 15 O'Leary volumes on archive.org, one web search of 2 Nov 2026. Bákula 1949, the Archivo del Libertador and Mondolfi's biography were not reached, so prior art is open.

human: WAINUT set the task (catalogue 1523) and the rules; the AI agents fetched the images, transcribed, built the table, read and checked. No target-specific human intervention, and no person has checked the reading against the images.
